prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose your pet's personality", "Select traits like playful, calm, or curious to shape how your pet behaves on desktop.", "Playful, Calm, Energetic, Cozy", "Continue to Adoption"]
1: ["Your pet is officially live on your desktop!", "Watch your pet walk around your screen and learn how to interact right away."]
2: ["Welcome to Desktop Pets", "Select how you would like to meet your new digital companion today.", "Preset companions vs custom AI creation"]
3: []
4: ["Signing in connects your existing desktop pets and adoption history safely to this device."]
5: ["Preparing your desktop pet canvas", "Setting up sprite animations and desktop window controls..."]
6: ["Choose your onboarding speed", "Quick pick adoption takes under 1 minute. Custom pet creation takes under 3 minutes."]
7: ["Upload your pet photo", "Drag and drop any clear front-facing image of your pet to generate your animated companion."]
8: ["Tip: Right-click your pet on desktop anytime to access controls or hide it."]
9: ["Notify me when pet is ready"]
